title: A formally smooth local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings is flat
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m_A)$ and $(B,\mathfrak m_B)$ be Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local rings and $\varphi:A\to B$ a local homomorphism ($\varphi(\mathfrak m_A)\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$), making $B$ an $A$-algebra. If $B$ is formally smooth over $A$ for the $\mathfrak m_B$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic], then $\varphi$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NP (lemma-formally-smooth-flat, line 9981) and its proof (lines 9988-10015). The source's hypothesis is Definition Tag 07NI (definition-formally-smooth-adic, line 9213), which is defined by the equivalent conditions (2)(a), (2)(b) of Lemma Tag 07EC (lemma-formally-smooth, line 9165); condition (2)(b), the discrete topology on A, is the condition of def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic

proof.text: Let $A^\wedge$ and $B^\wedge$ be the completions of $A$ and $B$ at their maximal ideals [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Since $A$ and $B$ are Noetherian, their maximal ideals are finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The completions are local rings with maximal ideals $\mathfrak m_AA^\wedge$ and $\mathfrak m_BB^\wedge$ [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], are Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], and are complete for those ideals [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal]. The induced local map $A^\wedge\to B^\wedge$ is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak m_BB^\wedge$-adic topology by [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-complete-source-target]. It therefore suffices first to prove the theorem for complete Noetherian local rings; Steps 2--5 do so.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 07NP, first sentence, citing Lemma 07ED and Algebra Lemma 0316

proof.text: Assume now that $A$ and $B$ are complete. By [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-flat-presentation], choose a commutative square of local homomorphisms $R\to S$, $R\twoheadrightarrow A$, $S\twoheadrightarrow B$, $A\to B$ in which $R,S$ are complete Noetherian local rings, the vertical maps are surjective, and $R\to S$ is flat. Put $I=\ker(R\to A)$; commutativity makes the composite $I\to S\to B$ zero, so the surjection $S\to B$ factors through a surjective homomorphism of $A$-algebras $q:S/IS\twoheadrightarrow B$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 07NP, 'Choose a commutative diagram ... as in Lemma 07NN ... Let I be the kernel of R -> A'

proof.text: The canonical map $S\otimes_RA\to S/IS$, $s\otimes a\mapsto s\widetilde a\bmod IS$ (where $\widetilde a$ is any lift of $a$ to $R$), is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change]. Since $S$ is flat over $R$, its base change $S\otimes_RA$ is flat over $A$ [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change]; transporting the module structure through this isomorphism, $S/IS$ is a flat $A$-module.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 07NP, parenthesis citing Algebra Lemma 00HI for base change of flatness

proof.text: The $A$-algebra surjection $q:S/IS\twoheadrightarrow B$ has an $A$-algebra section. Indeed, $S/IS$ is a complete Noetherian local ring by [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-quotient]. Let $C=S/IS$ and $J=\ker q$. Because $q:C\to B$ is a surjective local homomorphism, $q^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)=\mathfrak m_C$ and surjectivity gives $q(\mathfrak m_C)=\mathfrak m_B$: the inclusion into $\mathfrak m_B$ is locality, while for $b\in\mathfrak m_B$ a lift $c\in C$ cannot be a unit, since then $b=q(c)$ would be a unit, so $c\in\mathfrak m_C$. Hence $q(\mathfrak m_C^n)=q(\mathfrak m_C)^n=\mathfrak m_B^n$ for every $n\ge1$. Therefore $q^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B^n)=J+\mathfrak m_C^n$: one inclusion is clear; if $q(c)=q(x)$ for some $x\in\mathfrak m_C^n$, then $c-x\in J$. Since the complete local ring $B$ is $\mathfrak m_B$-adically separated, $\bigcap_{n\ge1}\mathfrak m_B^n=0$, and consequently $\bigcap_{n\ge1}(J+\mathfrak m_C^n)=q^{-1}(\bigcap_{n\ge1}\mathfrak m_B^n)=J$. Thus $J$ is closed for the $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology; also $J\subseteq\mathfrak m_C$. The identity map $B\to C/J\cong B$ is continuous because it sends $\mathfrak m_B$ into $q(\mathfrak m_C)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-lift-into-complete] with target $C$, ideal of definition $\mathfrak m_C$, closed ideal $J$, and $t=1$ to lift that identity to an $A$-algebra map $s:B\to C$ satisfying $q\circ s=\operatorname{id}_B$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 07NP, 'Because B is formally smooth over A ... S/IS -> B has a section, see Lemma 07NJ'

proof.text: The $A$-linear maps $s:B\to S/IS$ and $q:S/IS\to B$ satisfy $q\circ s=\operatorname{id}_B$ by Step 4. Thus $B$ is a retract of the flat $A$-module $S/IS$ from Step 3, and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-retract] shows that $B$ is flat over $A$. This proves the complete case.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 07NP, final sentence, 'Hence B is a direct summand of the flat A-module S/IS ... whence flat'

proof.text: Return to the original $A$ and $B$. Steps 1--5 show that $A^\wedge\to B^\wedge$ is flat. The completion map $A\to A^\wedge$ is flat and $B\to B^\wedge$ is faithfully flat [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat]. Hence the composite $A\to A^\wedge\to B^\wedge$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp]. Regarding $B^\wedge$ as a $B$-module through $B\to B^\wedge$, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-permanence] applies: it is flat over $A$ and faithfully flat over $B$, so $A\to B$ is flat.
